docs.title: ProctorIDE documentation
docs.text:
ProctorIDE is an invitation-based academic platform that combines a web IDE (editing, version history, code execution) with activity-specific integrity controls and instructor workflows for courses that use coding assignments, projects, practice challenges, quizzes, and high-stakes tests or exams.

This site is the single source of truth for:

  • How to complete tasks (students, instructors, administrators)
  • End-to-end workflows by activity type
  • Transparency about what the platform records and who can see it
  • Operational procedures and compliance-oriented reference material (not legal advice)

Not legal advice

Compliance pages describe common practices and product behavior. Your institution’s counsel and privacy office should review final policies, DPAs, and notices.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Transparency first — Students should understand monitoring before starting each activity type (tracking overview).
  2. Least privilege — Access follows role (roles reference).
  3. UTC everywhere — Stored timestamps use UTC; configure hosts with TZ=UTC in production.
  4. Human review for high stakes — Automated signals support instructors; policy for grading and integrity decisions remains institutional.

docs.title: Build this documentation locally
docs.text:
From the proctor-ide app directory:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve

Open the URL shown (usually http://127.0.0.1:8000).

To publish a static site:

mkdocs build
# output in site/

docs.title: Compliance hub
docs.text:
Material for privacy, security, and accessibility stakeholders. Not legal advice—your counsel and privacy office must approve notices and agreements.

Topic Purpose Privacy overview High-level processing narrative. Education records (FERPA-oriented) US higher-ed framing (adapt for your region). Security controls Technical and administrative measures. Audit expectations What auditors may ask for. Accessibility WCAG-oriented expectations for the UI. Disclaimer Scope limits of this documentation.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
Courseware should be usable by learners with diverse abilities. For the web IDE:

  • Keyboard navigation for editor and primary actions (subject to Monaco/editor limits).
  • Sufficient contrast in themes; avoid color-only status cues where possible.
  • Screen reader: complex IDE surfaces remain challenging—offer documented alternatives (extended time, alternate format) per disability services.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• Track WCAG targets with your institution’s digital accessibility office.
  • File issues for blocking defects (cannot submit, cannot read errors).

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Student troubleshooting

docs.title: Audit expectations
docs.text: Auditors (internal IT, risk, or external assessors) typically ask for evidence that controls exist and operate.

docs.title: Common evidence artifacts
docs.text: Control area Example evidence Access IAM export, quarterly access reviews notes. Change management PR history, CI green builds, deployment logs. Logging Centralized API logs with retention matching policy. Vendor risk Current subprocessor list, DPAs. Training Instructor integrity training records (outside this repo).

docs.title: Student-facing integrity
docs.text:
• Syllabus language aligned with Transparency.
  • Samples of disclosure banners shown before exams.

docs.title: AI tools
docs.text: If assistants are enabled, document data flows and contracts—see AI assistant.

docs.title: Documentation scope
docs.text:
This MkDocs site describes intended behavior of the ProctorIDE application and recommended operational practices. It does not:

  • Constitute legal advice, regulatory guidance, or a warranty of fitness for a particular compliance regime.
  • Replace your institution’s privacy notices, honor code, or syllabus language.
  • Guarantee feature availability in every deployment or fork.

docs.title: Liability
docs.text: Open-source and internal documentation are provided as-is. Operators remain responsible for configuration, monitoring, and incident response.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text: Product behavior evolves; prefer version-controlled docs plus release notes (changelog) when investigating incidents.

docs.title: Education records (FERPA-oriented framing)
docs.text:
Jurisdiction

This page uses United States higher-ed concepts (FERPA) as a familiar anchor. Institutions outside the US should map to GDPR, PIPEDA, local education privacy laws, etc.

docs.title: Likely “education records” in scope
docs.text: When ProctorIDE stores personally identifiable student work, grades, or integrity artifacts tied to an enrolled learner, your registrar / privacy office may classify those as education records under FERPA—subject to school official exceptions, directory information rules, and consent requirements.

docs.title: School official / contractor
docs.text:
If a vendor processes records on behalf of the institution for legitimate educational interests, institutions typically need:

  • A written agreement with FERPA commitments.
  • Direct control over maintenance and redisclosure limits.

docs.title: Directory information
docs.text: Email addresses may or may not be directory information—do not assume.

docs.title: Student requests
docs.text: Route to Data requests.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: This page is not legal advice. Your counsel approves all DPAs and notices.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• Students submit coursework and may generate telemetry in integrity modes.
  • Instructors / TAs access learner data for educational purposes tied to their courses.
  • Administrators operate infrastructure and must follow least privilege.

docs.title: Processing purposes
docs.text:
• Deliver instruction: hosting files, running code, grading.
  • Integrity: deter and investigate misconduct where permitted by policy.
  • Operations: reliability, security monitoring, support.

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text: Link students to Data collected and Tracking by activity type from your syllabus.

docs.title: International transfers
docs.text: If users are in multiple regions, document transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy) with your vendors—especially Firebase / Google and your cloud region.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Vendors & subprocessors

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• TLS for browser ↔ API; wss:// for WebSockets in production.
  • Avoid mixed content that downgrades to insecure HTTP.

docs.title: Authentication & authorization
docs.text:
• Firebase ID tokens verified on the API (not trusting client-provided user ids for sensitive paths).
  • Role-based access for instructor vs student operations (roles).
  • Run logs and similar endpoints filter by authenticated identity.

docs.title: Data layer
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL with TIMESTAMPTZ for audit clarity.
  • Migrations via Alembic; test on staging before production.

docs.title: Execution isolation
docs.text: • Student code runs in sandbox services (e.g. Judge0), not on the API host.

docs.title: Hardening backlog (operators)
docs.text:
• Tighten CORS from * to known frontend origins in production.
  • Workspace path traversal reviews for multi-tenant filesystem access.
  • Ensure tracking endpoints bind student_id to the token, not client-supplied ids.

docs.text: • Incident response

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This section covers first login, supported environments, and terms used across ProctorIDE docs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Account: Invitations are issued by your instructor or institution; you sign in with Firebase Authentication (e.g. Google) unless your school configures otherwise.
  • Browser: Desktop Chromium-based or Firefox recommended for the MVP; follow Environments for details.
  • Network: Outbound HTTPS to the API; WebSocket access for real-time features (e.g. comments) as allowed by your school.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
1. Account & access — invites, roles, first sign-in.
  2. Environments — browser, OS, network.
  3. Glossary — activities, tracking levels, workspace.

docs.title: How access works
docs.text: ProctorIDE is invitation-oriented. Your institution or instructor controls who can join and which role you receive.

docs.title: Typical flow
docs.text:
1. You receive an invitation (link or code) or are enrolled on a roster that your school syncs.
  2. You sign in with the identity provider your course uses (commonly Google via Firebase Auth).
  3. The platform assigns a role and shows only the activities you are entitled to see.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Capabilities (summary) Student View dashboard, open enrolled activities, use the IDE, submit work, see own run logs (per product policy). TA Student capabilities for assigned courses, plus instructor-style tools where enabled (enrollment, review, monitoring). Instructor Create and configure activities, manage templates, enroll students, view submissions and integrity-related signals.

Details: Roles & permissions.

docs.title: Invitations (codes and email)
docs.text:
• Create (instructor/TA): invitations are generated in the product; each has an expiry and can be revoked.
  • Redeem (student): you redeem while signed in; the system records which account used the code.
  • Validate (optional): a “check code” step may be offered before sign-in to confirm the invite is still valid.

One person, one account

Use the identity your school expects. Switching accounts mid-course can break enrollment links.

docs.title: First sign-in checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Complete sign-in with the required provider.
  • [ ] Confirm your name and email match what the course expects.
  • [ ] Open the Dashboard and verify you see the right course or section.
  • [ ] Read the transparency or integrity notice for the first activity you start.

docs.title: If you cannot sign in
docs.text:
• Wrong school account: try the Google profile your syllabus lists.
  • Invite expired or revoked: contact your instructor or IT.
  • “Configuration” or 503 errors: the deployment may be missing Firebase admin configuration on the server—escalate to your admin with the time of the error.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Transparency: what we record
  • Troubleshooting (students)

docs.title: Supported client (MVP)
docs.text: Area Guidance Form factor Desktop browser; mobile support may be limited in early releases. Browsers Latest Chrome, Edge, or Firefox. Safari is best-effort. JavaScript Must be enabled (the IDE and dashboard are single-page applications). Pop-ups Not required for core flows; if your school uses a third-party auth pop-up, allow it.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
Requirement Why HTTPS to the ProctorIDE API All REST calls and auth. WebSocket to the same API host (if used) Real-time comments; some networks block ws://—production should use wss://. Outbound to execution service Code runs on the backend (e.g. Judge0); you do not need a local compiler.

Locked-down labs

School IT may need to allow your production API domain and WebSocket (or wss://) to the same host. Provide them the base URL and that you use standard ports 443.

docs.title: Time and locale
docs.text:
• The platform stores UTC internally. Due times and logs should be shown in a sensible local or course timezone in the UI as the product matures; until then, treat due dates as specified in the syllabus.
  • Set server TZ=UTC in deployment to avoid skew in logs (see Admin deployment).

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text: • Target: WCAG-oriented components; see Accessibility statement for scope and how to report issues.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Activity A unit of work in a course: assignment, project, challenge, quiz, test, or exam. Each has a type and tracking level. Assignment Longer-form work; often moderate tracking (edits, run events, version history). Project Multi-file or longer effort; may share the same product path as an assignment with different rubric in the syllabus. Challenge Low-stakes practice; typically minimal tracking. Quiz Shorter assessment; basic integrity (time, focus, paste in some designs). Test / exam High-stakes; comprehensive tracking; may add proctoring features as your institution enables them. Tracking level Configured intensity of behavioral and technical logging (see matrix). Workspace Your isolated file area for an activity; version history is stored on the server; you do not use raw Git commands. Timeline History of saved versions (backed by the platform’s version control), used for recovery and review. Run Executing code in a sandbox (e.g. Judge0) and returning output; runs can be logged for integrity. Invitation A code or link that grants access with a role and expiry. Enrollment Association between a student and an activity (and status: not started, in progress, submitted, etc.). FERPA (US) Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act; governs access to education records in U.S. schools. This doc set uses a practical framing only—see disclaimer.

docs.title: Deploy or upgrade
docs.text:
Follow Deployment and Migration notes.

Checklist:

  1. Apply database migrations (alembic upgrade head) in staging, then production.
  2. Deploy API with correct DATABASE_URL, Firebase credentials, and Judge0 (or equivalent) URL.
  3. Deploy frontend with VITE_* variables pointing at the production API.
  4. Confirm /health and a smoke test (sign-in + list activities).

docs.title: Rotate secrets
docs.text:
• Firebase service account JSON: replace file on API hosts, restart workers.
  • Database credentials: rotate in secret manager and update DATABASE_URL; avoid downtime with connection pool reload where supported.

docs.title: Respond to incidents
docs.text: Use Incident response; preserve logs per retention policy.

docs.title: Vendor due diligence
docs.text: Maintain Vendors & subprocessors when adding OAuth IdPs, hosting regions, or analytics.

docs.title: Create an activity
docs.text:
1. Open the teacher admin area (exact UI label may vary by deployment).
  2. Choose activity type (assignment, challenge, quiz, exam)—this drives tracking intensity (matrix).
  3. Set title, due date, and visibility per course policy.
  4. Upload a starter template or attach files so students begin from a consistent baseline.

docs.title: Enroll students
docs.text:
1. Generate invitations (single or bulk) from the enrollment workflow (Enrollment).
  2. Share codes through your LMS or syllabus—avoid posting restricted codes in public channels.

docs.title: Monitor progress
docs.text:
• Use submissions and activity views described in Monitoring & review.
  • Run logs and tracking events visibility follows role (Instructor visibility).

docs.title: Grade or review
docs.text:
• Align rubrics with what the platform automatically captures vs what requires human judgment.
  • Document integrity concerns using institutional procedures, not ad-hoc screenshots alone—see Incident response.

docs.title: Collaboration comments
docs.text: • When enabled, comments attach to lines of code; moderate tone per course policy.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text: Use the identity method your instructor specifies (often school Google / Microsoft). If sign-in fails repeatedly, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Find your work
docs.text: Open the dashboard, locate the activity, then Start or Continue.

docs.title: Work in the IDE
docs.text:
• Edit files in the browser IDE; save often.
  • Use Run to execute code in the course sandbox; read stderr when builds fail.
  • Use Timeline to restore earlier versions when allowed (Timeline).

docs.title: Understand monitoring
docs.text: Before high-stakes activities, read Tracking by activity type and Data collected.

docs.title: Submit
docs.text: Use Submit when your attempt is final unless your instructor allows multiple submissions.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text:
• Technical: instructor or campus IT with timestamps and error text (no secrets).
  • Grade disputes: follow your syllabus’s regrade process.

docs.title: Operational procedures
docs.text:
These procedures support security, privacy, and continuity for institutions running ProctorIDE.

Procedure When to use Incident response Suspected breach, outage, or data leak. Access reviews Periodic verification of admin and instructor privileges. Data requests Student or parent requests; subpoenas—coordinate with legal. Retention Align backups and databases with policy. Vendors & subprocessors Onboarding IdPs, hosting, AI tools, analytics. Testing policy How the engineering team validates releases (CI, manual smoke).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Review quarterly (or per campus policy):

  • Cloud project owners and IAM bindings (Firebase, GCP, database admin).
  • Repository admins for this codebase.
  • Production secrets distribution list.

docs.title: Instructor / TA access
docs.text:
• Confirm staff lost access when courses end.
  • Prefer course-scoped roles over global superuser accounts.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Keep a lightweight log: date, reviewer, systems checked, follow-ups.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Roles & permissions

docs.title: Data requests (students, parents, legal)
docs.text:
Not legal advice

Coordinate all formal requests with your privacy office and counsel.

docs.title: Student access / correction
docs.text:
Many institutions provide portals for education records access. For ProctorIDE-hosted data:

  1. Identify the subject (verified identity).
  2. Locate records: database queries by UID / email per schema.
  3. Export in a common format (CSV/PDF of submissions) where feasible.
  4. Respond within institutional timelines.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text:
• Course completion may still require retention for grades disputes—do not delete blindly.
  • Anonymization may satisfy some policies when raw deletion conflicts with transcripts.

docs.title: Law enforcement / subpoenas
docs.text: • Route through legal; preserve chain of custody for logs.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Education records · Retention

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
• Availability: API or database unavailable beyond SLA.
  • Integrity: suspected token leak, privilege escalation, or mass data export.
  • Privacy: accidental exposure of another student’s work or grades.

docs.title: Immediate actions
docs.text:
1. Contain: rotate compromised credentials; disable affected invitations if abuse is invitation-based.
  2. Preserve: snapshot logs (access-controlled); avoid destructive DB operations until scope is known.
  3. Notify: internal security / legal per institutional policy; do not promise specifics publicly until confirmed.

docs.title: Product-specific notes
docs.text:
• Firebase: revoke leaked tokens at IdP if applicable; review Admin SDK key exposure.
  • PostgreSQL: identify time window from TIMESTAMPTZ audit columns.

docs.title: After resolution
docs.text:
• Document root cause and corrective actions.
  • Update Vendors if a vendor contributed.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Security controls

docs.title: Data retention
docs.text: Retention must match institutional policy, accreditation, and regulatory requirements in your jurisdiction.

docs.title: Engineering defaults (configure explicitly)
docs.text: Data class Typical guidance Grades / submissions Retain per registrar policy (often years). Integrity telemetry Shorter than submissions unless integrity investigation requires longer hold. Server logs Weeks to months in hot storage; archive or delete per infra policy. Backups Align restore goals with deletion—orphaned backups are a common gap.

docs.title: UTC timestamps
docs.text: The stack stores timestamps in UTC (TIMESTAMPTZ in PostgreSQL after migration 0002). Use UTC when defining cutover jobs for purge scripts.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Migration notes

docs.title: Testing policy (engineering)
docs.text: This document describes how ProctorIDE is validated in development—distinct from academic integrity “testing” of students.

docs.title: Automated tests
docs.text:
• Backend: pytest under backend/tests/ against a SQLite test database for fast CI.
  • CI: GitHub Actions workflow runs tests on push/PR (see .github/workflows/ci.yml).

docs.title: What CI does not guarantee
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL-only behaviors (some migrations are no-ops on SQLite)—run alembic upgrade head against staging Postgres before production.
  • Firebase end-to-end flows without configured credentials.
  • Judge0 availability or language runtime parity.

docs.title: Manual smoke (recommended each release)
docs.text:
1. Sign in with a test tenant user.
  2. List activities, open workspace, save a file.
  3. Run code; confirm console output.
  4. Open WebSocket comments with a valid token (query param in dev).
  5. Verify role-scoped run logs (student vs instructor).

docs.title: Local dev tokens
docs.text: Some deployments support dev-{role} tokens for local development only—never enable in production.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• How-to for admins
  • Accessibility for UI regression checks

docs.title: Vendors and subprocessors
docs.text: Maintain a live register of organizations that process personal data on behalf of your deployment.

docs.title: Common candidates for this stack
docs.text: Vendor / service Typical role Firebase (Google) Authentication; token verification via Admin SDK. Cloud host (e.g. Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL) Runtime and database. Judge0 (or equivalent) Sandboxed code execution; receives source code transiently. Email / LMS Invitation delivery—if integrated.

docs.title: When to update
docs.text:
• Changing region or data residency.
  • Enabling AI features that send prompts outside your VPC.
  • Adding error tracking (Sentry, etc.) that captures PII.

docs.title: Contract checklist
docs.text:
• DPA / FERPA alignment where applicable.
  • Subprocessor notification clauses if you add vendors mid-term.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Privacy overview

docs.title: Reference overview
docs.text:
Quick lookups for activity behavior, permissions, HTTP/WebSocket API, and FAQ.

Page Description Activity types matrix Tracking vs type at a glance. Roles & permissions Student, TA, instructor, admin. API overview REST + WebSocket routes (prefix /api). FAQ Common questions.

docs.title: Activity types matrix
docs.text:
Compact reference aligned with Tracking by activity type.

Type Typical stakes IDE depth Tracking tier Challenge Low (practice) Full Minimal Quiz Medium-low Moderate Basic Assignment / project Medium-high Full Moderate Test / exam High Full + tight rules Comprehensive

docs.title: Configuration knobs
docs.text: Instructors may still adjust due dates, files, and collaboration—always document exceptions in the syllabus.

docs.title: API overview
docs.text: Base URL shown as {API}. Authenticated routes expect Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token> unless noted.

docs.title: Health
docs.text: Method Path Notes GET {API}/health Liveness probe.

docs.title: Auth (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes POST /api/auth/verify-token Validate token / bootstrap session patterns. GET /api/auth/me Current user profile from verified token.

docs.title: Invitations (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes POST /api/invitations Create invitation. GET /api/invitations List invitations (scoped by role). POST /api/invitations/bulk Bulk create. GET /api/invitations/validate/{code} Pre-flight validation. POST /api/invitations/redeem Redeem code → enrollment. POST /api/invitations/{code}/revoke Revoke code.

docs.title: Activities (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes POST /api/activities Create activity. GET /api/activities List activities for user. POST /api/activities/{activity_id}/start Start session. POST /api/activities/{activity_id}/submit Submit attempt. POST /api/activities/{activity_id}/template Attach template. POST /api/activities/{activity_id}/template-files Multi-file template upload. POST /api/activities/{activity_id}/enroll Enroll user. GET /api/activities/{activity_id}/submissions List submissions (instructor/TA).

docs.title: Workspace (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes GET /api/workspace/{workspace_id}/files List or fetch file tree. PUT /api/workspace/{workspace_id}/files/{path} Write file (path is path segment). GET /api/workspace/{workspace_id}/log Version / commit log. POST /api/workspace/{workspace_id}/restore/{commit_id} Restore snapshot.

docs.title: Execution (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes POST /api/run Run code via sandbox (e.g. Judge0); auth required; logs include user. GET /api/run/logs Role-filtered run logs (student: own; instructor/TA: broader).

docs.title: Tracking (/api)
docs.text: Method Path Notes POST /api/tracking/events Ingest integrity/telemetry events. GET /api/tracking/events Query events (role-scoped).

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text: URL Notes wss://{host}/api/ws/comments/{activity_id}?token=... Real-time comments; token must be verified server-side.

docs.title: CORS
docs.text: Default dev server may allow all origins—tighten in production to your SPA origin.

docs.title: Why can I not see other students’ work?
docs.text: The platform enforces privacy and integrity—submissions are visible only to you and authorized staff.

docs.title: Are my keystrokes recorded?
docs.text: Maybe, depending on activity type and course settings. Read Tracking by activity type before starting.

docs.title: Is my code run on my laptop?
docs.text: Execution goes through a server-side sandbox (e.g. Judge0). You should assume staff can see source and output you run through the product.

docs.title: Can I export submissions?
docs.text: Use your deployment’s export or database tools consistent with Retention and Data requests.

docs.title: TAs see too much / too little
docs.text: Map enrollment and role configuration; see Roles & permissions.

docs.title: SQLite vs PostgreSQL in CI?
docs.text: Tests often use SQLite for speed; run Alembic against Postgres in staging because some migrations are no-ops on SQLite—see Testing policy.

docs.title: Where is UTC configured?
docs.text: Set TZ=UTC on servers; DB uses TIMESTAMPTZ after migration 0002—see Migration notes.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Typical capabilities Student View enrolled activities; edit own workspace; run code; submit; see own restricted logs where exposed by API policy. TA Instructor-like access within assigned courses/activities (deployment-dependent enrollment). Instructor Create activities; enroll; view submissions and integrity tooling for own sections. Administrator Infrastructure, secrets, global configuration—not course grading unless also enrolled as staff.

docs.title: API enforcement
docs.text: Sensitive routes require Bearer token verification via Firebase. WebSockets (comments) should pass token= in the query string and derive identity only from verified claims—not client user_id.

docs.title: Principle
docs.text: Least privilege: grant TA the minimum scope needed for grading assistance.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to the application and documentation are tracked here at a high level. For file-level history, use git log.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• Documentation: complete MkDocs How-to, Transparency, Procedures, Compliance, Reference, and Releases sections.
  • Backend: lifespan startup; UTC-aware datetimes; role-scoped run logs; WebSocket auth via verified token.
  • Database: Alembic 0002 for PostgreSQL TIMESTAMPTZ columns (no-op on SQLite test DB).

docs.title: 0.1.0 — Initial integrated stack
docs.text:
• Monorepo: Vite + React frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, Judge0 execution, Firebase auth, GitPython workspaces.
  • Core flows: invitations, activities, workspace, run, tracking hooks, collaboration WebSocket.

For deployment upgrade steps, see Migration notes.

docs.title: Alembic 0002 — datetime timezone awareness
docs.text:
Purpose: Align ORM and PostgreSQL with UTC using TIMESTAMPTZ for time columns where applicable.

Environment Effect PostgreSQL Columns migrated to timestamp with time zone; store and compare in UTC. SQLite (tests) Often a no-op or compatible mapping—continue to run pytest locally.

docs.title: Operator checklist
docs.text:
1. Backup production database before migration.
  2. Apply on staging: alembic upgrade head.
  3. Set TZ=UTC on API workers and verify invitation/expiry behavior.

docs.title: Application expectations
docs.text:
• Prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc) (or shared helpers) over naive utcnow() for new code.
  • Invitation expiry comparisons should tolerate legacy naive rows until backfilled (product uses UTC helpers).

docs.title: Firebase / auth
docs.text:
When rotating service account JSON:

  1. Deploy new secret.
  2. Restart API instances before revoking old keys.
  3. Smoke-test sign-in, run, and WebSocket comments.

docs.title: Transparency hub
docs.text: ProctorIDE is designed so students, instructors, and institutions can understand what is recorded, why, and who can access it.

docs.title: Core topics
docs.text: Topic Description Tracking by activity type How monitoring intensity maps to assignment vs exam. Data collected Categories of telemetry and artifacts. Data not collected Boundaries and common misconceptions. Student visibility What learners can see about their own data. Instructor visibility What teaching staff can see. AI assistant If your deployment integrates coding assistants—expectations and constraints.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Disclose before high stakes — Students should see clear notices before starting exams when tracking is strong.
  2. Least privilege — Access matches roles.
  3. Institutional policy wins — Product defaults do not replace your school’s integrity code or privacy notices.

Note

This documentation describes typical product behavior. Your deployment may enable or disable features; confirm with your administrator.

docs.title: AI assistant — transparency and exploration
docs.text: Some courses integrate AI coding assistants (IDE plugins, campus-wide licenses, or embedded chat). This page frames expectations when AI touches assessment workflows.

docs.title: Institutional stance comes first
docs.text:
Your syllabus should state whether AI assistance is:

  • Allowed with citation,
  • Limited (e.g. explanations only, no full solutions),
  • Prohibited for graded work.

The platform does not replace honor-code enforcement—instructors define rules.

docs.title: Data implications
docs.text:
If students use an external assistant:

  • Prompts and code may leave the institution’s boundary—treat as third-party processing.
  • Update Vendors & subprocessors when introducing new AI tools.

If the product embeds an assistant:

  • Expect logging similar to other editor actions where integrity modes apply.
  • Students should receive clear notice before the assistant sends context off-device.

docs.title: Pedagogy
docs.text:
• Prefer formative challenges with AI allowed before summative exams with AI restricted.
  • Design tasks that reward process artifacts (tests, explanations) that are harder to fake.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Audit expectations
  • Testing policy

docs.title: Data collected — overview
docs.text: This page summarizes categories of data the platform may process. Not every category applies to every activity or deployment.

docs.title: Identity and access
docs.text:
• Authentication provider subject (e.g. Firebase UID), email when exposed by the IdP and stored by policy.
  • Invitation codes and role (student, TA, instructor) after redemption.

docs.title: Course and activity data
docs.text:
• Activity metadata: title, type, due dates, enrollment links.
  • Submissions and workspace file contents for graded work.
  • Git-like history: commits or snapshots for recovery and integrity review.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text:
• Run requests (language, source sent to sandbox).
  • Stdout/stderr, exit status, and timestamps from the execution service (e.g. Judge0).
  • Server-side run logs may include the authenticated user id for audit trails.

docs.title: Behavioral telemetry (when enabled)
docs.text:
• Tracking events such as keystroke bursts, clipboard operations, focus/blur—gated by activity type in the product design.
  • Events are stored for review workflows, not for sale.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text: • Comments on code lines, author identity, timestamps.

docs.title: Technical diagnostics
docs.text:
• HTTP logs, error traces on servers (often excluding full request bodies in production).
  • WebSocket connection metadata for real-time features.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Data not collected · Retention

docs.title: Data not collected — boundaries
docs.text: Use this page to set expectations and avoid miscommunication with students and privacy reviewers.

docs.title: Not collected by the core product (typical)
docs.text:
The following are not standard features of the open-source ProctorIDE stack described in this repo unless explicitly integrated by your institution:

  • Continuous webcam or screen video (unless you add a separate proctoring vendor).
  • Microphone audio streams for surveillance.
  • Keylogging outside the IDE surface (OS-wide keyloggers are out of scope).
  • Browser history unrelated to the assessment session.
  • Personal files on the student device outside uploaded workspace paths.

docs.title: Execution sandbox
docs.text: • Code is executed in a service-controlled environment (e.g. Judge0). Students should assume instructors and systems can see submitted source and run output—not “private” execution on a personal laptop.

docs.title: Third parties
docs.text: If your school adds analytics, AI assistants, or LMS deep links, those vendors may introduce additional processing—document them in Vendors & subprocessors.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Privacy overview

docs.title: Tracking by activity type
docs.text: Activity type drives default integrity monitoring intensity. Exact behavior depends on course configuration and product version—verify in your deployment.

docs.title: Summary matrix
docs.text: Activity type Typical monitoring Rationale Challenge Light Practice and experimentation; lower stakes. Quiz Basic Short assessments; time and focus signals often enabled. Assignment / project Moderate Full IDE use; version history and run logs common. Test / exam Comprehensive Strongest signals and tightest rules per institutional policy.

docs.title: What “stronger” monitoring can include
docs.text:
Examples that may apply in exam modes (not all are guaranteed in every build):

  • Editor events: keystrokes, paste/cut, focus changes (where implemented).
  • Execution: command runs, stdout/stderr through the sandbox (data collected).
  • Session metadata: timestamps in UTC for correlation.

docs.title: Instructor responsibility
docs.text:
• Choose the lowest adequate integrity level for the learning goal.
  • Align disclosures with your syllabus and accessibility office.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Activity types matrix

docs.title: Instructor and TA visibility
docs.text: Teaching staff use aggregated and per-student views to grade, support, and investigate integrity concerns.

docs.title: Typical access
docs.text:
• Roster / enrollment for activities they manage.
  • Submissions and files for those activities.
  • Execution logs and tracking events where enabled by activity type.
  • Comment threads on student code.

docs.title: Least privilege
docs.text:
• TAs receive permissions your institution configures—do not assume global admin access.
  • Cross-course access should be denied unless staff are explicitly enrolled or given admin roles.

docs.title: Audit posture
docs.text: Access for grading should be documented (who graded whom). High-stakes integrity reviews should follow Incident response.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Roles & permissions

docs.title: Student visibility of data
docs.text: Students should be able to understand what exists about them and how to request corrections under institutional policy.

docs.title: Generally visible to the student
docs.text:
• Their own submissions and IDE workspace state for active activities.
  • Run output from their own executions in the console UI.
  • Their comment history where collaboration is enabled.

docs.title: May be limited during exams
docs.text: • Full instructor analytics and integrity timelines may be hidden until after the exam window—deployment-dependent.

docs.title: Run logs (API)
docs.text:
In hardened deployments, GET /api/run/logs returns:

  • Students: rows associated with their user id.
  • Instructors / TAs: broader visibility per role policy.

If you see empty logs, your role or activity policy may restrict the view.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Data requests

docs.title: Workflows overview
docs.text: Workflow documentation is split by persona. Each path describes happy paths, exceptions, and pointers to transparency and compliance topics.

docs.title: Instructor / TA
docs.text:
Start at Instructor hub. Typical sequences:

  1. Create activity → set type and tracking → upload template → enroll → monitor → review submissions.

docs.title: Student
docs.text:
Start at Student hub. Typical sequences:

  1. Dashboard → acknowledge transparency if shown → start activity → edit/run → submit.

docs.title: Administrator / IT
docs.text: Start at Admin hub for deployment, networking, and secrets.

docs.title: Administrator workflows — overview
docs.text: Administrators deploy and operate ProctorIDE so instructors and students have a reliable, secure, and auditable experience.

docs.title: Operational cadence
docs.text: Frequency Task Weekly Review error budgets / logs in hosting platform. Monthly Access review for admin roles (procedure). Quarterly Update subprocessors and retention alignment.

docs.text: Component Role Frontend Static SPA (e.g. Vite build behind nginx or CDN). API FastAPI backend. PostgreSQL Primary datastore (TIMESTAMPTZ after migration 0002). Judge0 (or equivalent) Sandboxed code execution. Firebase End-user authentication; Admin SDK on server for token verification.

See repository .env.example for authoritative names. Typical:

  • TZ=UTC — recommended on servers.

docs.title: Instructor and TA workflows — overview
docs.text: Instructors and teaching assistants use ProctorIDE to design assessments, deliver them to the right students, observe integrity-aligned signals, and review submissions.

docs.title: Core lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Create activity] --> B[Configure type & tracking]
  B --> C[Upload template / starter]
  C --> D[Enroll students]
  D --> E[Students work]
  E --> F[Monitor & review]
  F --> G[Grade / feedback]

Detailed: Activity lifecycle.

docs.title: Guides by task
docs.text: Goal Document Long homework / multi-file Assignments & projects Practice sets Challenges Short checks Quizzes High-stakes Tests & exams Rosters and codes Enrollment Starter repos / files Templates During / after Monitoring & review

docs.title: Transparency obligation
docs.text: Before students begin work, they should see what is monitored for that activity type. Align your syllabus language with Tracking by activity type.

docs.title: Compliance reminders
docs.text:
• Only grant TA or instructor roles to people covered by your institution’s policies.
  • Export/deletion requests follow Data requests once your deployment registers a process.

docs.title: Instructor workflow — activity lifecycle
docs.text: This page describes the intended lifecycle from authoring through review. Exact UI labels may evolve; the order of operations stays stable.

docs.title: 1. Plan
docs.text:
• Choose activity type (assignment, project, challenge, quiz, test, exam).
  • Choose tracking level consistent with your syllabus and institutional policy (see matrix).
  • Decide due date and late policy (communicated outside or inside the product as available).

docs.title: 2. Create
docs.text:
• Create the activity in the Teacher or admin UI (or API if automated).
  • Record the internal activity ID if you integrate tools or docs.

docs.title: 3. Configure integrity / transparency
docs.text:
• Ensure students will see the correct pre-start disclosure for this type.
  • For exams, confirm whether additional proctoring (camera, lockdown) is in scope for your deployment—not all features ship in every release.

docs.title: 4. Upload template
docs.text:
• Provide starter files and ASSIGNMENT.md (or equivalent) so the IDE opens with clear instructions.
  • See Templates.

docs.title: 5. Enroll
docs.text:
• Add students by invitation or bulk UID list as supported.
  • Verify enrollments before the due date.
  • See Enrollment.

docs.title: 6. Monitor (optional but recommended)
docs.text:
• Watch submission status and integrity signals appropriate to the activity type.
  • See Monitoring & review.

docs.title: 7. Review and grade
docs.text:
• Open submissions (files, timeline, run logs per policy).
  • Apply your rubric; ProctorIDE provides artifacts, not automatic final grades unless you add external tooling.

docs.title: 8. Archive
docs.text: • Follow your institution’s retention policy; see Retention.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Assignments & projects
  • Tests & exams
  • Transparency hub

docs.title: Instructor workflow — assignments and projects
docs.text: Assignments and projects are the primary vehicles for sustained coding work: multiple files, iterative runs, and rich version history.

docs.title: Pedagogical intent
docs.text:
• Students learn through draft → run → revise.
  • You want moderate integrity signals: enough to deter misconduct and explain anomalies, without pretending to replace human judgment.

docs.title: Configuration checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Activity type set to assignment or project (as your product enumerates).
  • [ ] Tracking level: typically moderate (see matrix).
  • [ ] Starter template includes clear success criteria (ASSIGNMENT.md).
  • [ ] Due date communicated (product + syllabus).
  • [ ] Late policy stated in syllabus; link or paste key rules in instructions.

docs.title: Delivery workflow
docs.text:
1. Upload template files (single file or multi-file).
  2. Enroll students.
  3. Optionally announce transparency: what is logged (saves, runs, edits summary).

docs.title: Review workflow
docs.text:
1. Open submissions list for the activity.
  2. For each student, review files, timeline (history of commits/saves), and run logs (per deployment policy).
  3. Compare against rubric; document anomalies using institutional process.

docs.title: Integrity notes
docs.text:
• Encourage students to cite permitted resources in comments when collaboration rules allow inline citations.
  • Run logs show execution attempts, not proof of authorship alone—pair with timeline and assessment design.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Templates
  • Monitoring
  • Student: IDE and submit

docs.title: Instructor workflow — challenges
docs.text: Challenges are typically low-stakes practice: experimentation, optional drills, or exploration.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Reduce anxiety and encourage volume of practice.
  • Keep tracking light so logs do not overwhelm instructors.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Tracking level: usually minimal (see matrix).
  • Clear labeling in the dashboard so students know this is practice, not a graded exam.

docs.title: Instructor workload
docs.text:
• Spot-check submissions only if you use challenges for participation credit.
  • Otherwise rely on auto-run success or completion markers if enabled.

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text: • Still disclose minimal logging in student-facing copy—practice does not mean “no logging,” but it should be proportionate.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Student: starting an activity
  • Tracking by activity

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Ensure only intended students can access an activity.
  • Maintain an audit-friendly trail of who was added and when.

docs.title: Methods (as implemented in your deployment)
docs.text:
1. Invitation codes or links — single-use or expiring; instructors generate and distribute securely.
  2. Bulk enrollment — paste or upload student identifiers your admin supports (often institutional UIDs mapped to accounts).

docs.title: Issue invitations
docs.text:
• Generate invites with correct role (student vs TA).
  • Set expiry aligned to add/drop deadlines.
  • Revoke unused invites after the deadline.

docs.title: Verify roster
docs.text: • Spot-check that enrolled students match the official roster from your LMS or registrar export.

docs.title: Drops and misconduct holds
docs.text: • Follow institutional rules for removing access vs preserving work product for appeals.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Account & access
  • Access reviews

docs.title: What “monitoring” means here
docs.text: Monitoring is technical and behavioral telemetry configured per activity—not a substitute for sound assessment design or human judgment.

docs.title: Signals you may have access to
docs.text:
Depending on activity type and deployment:

  • Submission status (not started / in progress / submitted).
  • Version timeline (history of saves/commits in the workspace).
  • Code execution logs (runs initiated from the IDE).
  • Integrity-oriented events (e.g. focus changes, paste-related markers when enabled)—see Tracking.

docs.title: Recommended review order
docs.text:
1. Confirm identity and enrollment.
  2. Read final submission and timeline for major anomalies.
  3. Examine run logs for impossible shortcuts vs the stated problem (interpret cautiously).
  4. Use institutional academic integrity process if you escalate.

docs.title: Privacy and minimization
docs.text:
• Access only what your role requires for the course.
  • Do not share raw logs publicly or with unauthorized peers.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Visibility (instructors)
  • Access reviews

docs.title: Instructor workflow — quizzes
docs.text: Quizzes are short, focused checks—often time-bounded—with basic integrity expectations.

docs.title: Design tips
docs.text:
• Keep prompts atomic (one concept per item when possible).
  • Align time limits with what a prepared student needs; document rounding rules for ties.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Tracking level: typically basic (focus changes, paste detection where enabled, time bounds).
  • Decide whether students can navigate backward between items (product capability permitting).

docs.title: Before students start
docs.text: • Publish integrity rules in the syllabus and reference the in-product transparency banner.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: • Use submission timestamps and basic signals; escalate anomalies per Incident response.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Quizzes from student side
  • Visibility (instructors)

docs.title: Instructor workflow — templates and starter code
Purpose
docs.text: Templates give every student a consistent starting point and reduce setup friction.

docs.title: Recommended contents
docs.text: File Purpose ASSIGNMENT.md Student-facing instructions, rubric summary, allowed resources Starter source files Minimal compilable/runnable skeleton Data files Small fixtures if needed (watch size limits)

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Keep templates small and scannable; link to longer readings externally if needed.
  • Avoid secrets (API keys); use environment placeholders documented in instructions.
  • Version templates in Git outside the LMS if you maintain a canonical repo; upload the release snapshot into ProctorIDE.

docs.title: After upload
docs.text: • Smoke-test by opening the activity as a sandbox student account if permitted.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Assignments & projects
  • Student: IDE

docs.title: Instructor workflow — tests and exams
docs.text: Tests and exams are high-stakes. ProctorIDE’s architecture supports stronger integrity signals; your institution decides which layers are enabled (technical monitoring, human proctoring, lockdown browsers, etc.).

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
• Clarify what is allowed: references, notes, IDE features, internet.
  • Align tracking level to comprehensive when using platform logging broadly.
  • Coordinate with testing center or online proctoring if applicable—the product may integrate signals but does not replace institutional exam policy.

docs.title: Configuration checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Activity labeled clearly as exam in the UI.
  • [ ] Due / availability window matches registrar or department rules.
  • [ ] Accommodations handled per disability services (extended time, breaks)—often manual overrides outside MVP scope.
  • [ ] Transparency: students must see a plain-language summary before starting.

docs.title: During the window
docs.text:
• Monitor for spikes in support tickets (auth, disconnects).
  • Have a communications channel (course forum) for technical escalation.

docs.title: After the window
docs.text:
• Lock submissions per policy.
  • Review integrity bundles: timeline, runs, tracking events as enabled.
  • Follow academic integrity due process—automated signals are not standalone proof.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Transparency: tracking
  • Incident response
  • FERPA-oriented framing

docs.title: Student workflows — overview
docs.text: Students use ProctorIDE to see what is due, work in a browser IDE with saved history, run code safely, and submit to their instructor.

docs.title: Golden path
docs.text:
1. Dashboard — find the activity.
  2. Start the activity — read any transparency notice.
  3. Use the IDE, run, submit — complete your work.
  4. Use Timeline to recover from mistakes.
  5. Comments if your course enables discussion on code lines.

docs.title: By activity type
docs.text: Type What to expect Assignment / project More files, more iterations, moderate logging of work patterns. Challenge Lighter logging; still follow course rules. Quiz Shorter, often stricter time or navigation rules. Test / exam Strongest monitoring; read disclosures carefully.

docs.title: If something breaks
docs.text: Troubleshooting — auth, network, run failures.

docs.title: Your rights and transparency
docs.text: Always review Transparency hub before assuming what is private.

docs.title: Student workflow — collaboration comments
docs.text: When enabled, you can attach comments to lines of code for discussion with instructors or TAs.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Real-time connections should use a secure token (e.g. Firebase ID token in the WebSocket URL in modern deployments).
  • Do not share your token with others.

docs.title: Conduct
docs.text: • Stay professional; comments may be retained per Retention.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Instructor monitoring

docs.title: Student workflow — dashboard
docs.text:
The dashboard lists activities you are enrolled in, usually with:

  • Title and type (assignment, quiz, exam, …).
  • Due date (when configured).
  • Status: not started, in progress, submitted, graded (labels vary).

docs.title: What you should do
docs.text:
1. Sort mentally by due date and stakes (exam before optional challenge).
  2. Click through to start or resume work.

docs.title: If an activity is missing
docs.text:
• Confirm you used the correct school account.
  • Ask your instructor whether enrollment completed.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Starting an activity

docs.title: Student workflow — IDE, run, and submit
Editor
docs.text:
• You edit files in a web IDE (Monaco-based in the product).
  • Save often; the platform may auto-save and keep a version history (see Timeline).
  • You do not run raw Git commands—history is managed for you.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
• Run sends code to a sandbox (e.g. Judge0) through the backend.
  • Output (stdout/stderr) appears in the console area.
  • Run logs may be retained for integrity—see Data collected.

docs.title: HTML / UI previews
docs.text: • Some courses use an HTML preview pane; interactive pages may be sandboxed in an iframe.

docs.title: Submit
docs.text:
• Use Submit when your work is final for that attempt (unless your instructor allows multiple attempts).
  • After submit, policy may lock editing—confirm in your syllabus.

docs.title: Fair use
docs.text: • Do not attempt to spoof identity or tamper with telemetry—your institution’s integrity policy applies.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Run logs visibility
  • How-to (students)

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
1. Read the transparency / integrity notice for this activity type if the product shows one.
  2. Close unnecessary applications if the notice says the exam is monitored more strictly.
  3. Ensure a stable network; reconnects may be logged as events in some modes.

docs.title: Start
docs.text: • Click Start (or equivalent). The platform records start time and may set status to in progress.

docs.title: During high-stakes sessions
docs.text:
• Follow your instructor’s rules on resources, collaboration, and second devices.
  • If you experience a technical failure, document the time and contact your instructor with a screenshot of any error (no personal data of other students).

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Tracking by activity type
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Student workflow — timeline and version history
Purpose
docs.text:
The timeline helps you:

  • Recover from accidental large deletes.
  • Understand how your solution evolved (useful when explaining work to a TA).

docs.title: How it works (conceptually)
docs.text: Each meaningful save may create a snapshot in the platform’s version store. You can browse prior versions and restore when permitted by activity rules.

docs.title: Exams
docs.text: • Restoration may be limited or disabled during or after the exam window—follow on-screen messages.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • Transparency

docs.title: Sign-in fails
docs.text:
• Use the identity provider your syllabus specifies (often school Google).
  • Clear site data only if IT recommends it; then retry incognito to rule out extensions.
  • If error mentions configuration, escalate to your instructor—server Firebase setup may be incomplete.

docs.title: “Cannot load activities”
docs.text:
• Check network/VPN.
  • Confirm enrollment.

docs.title: Code run fails or times out
docs.text:
• Read stderr; fix compile errors first.
  • If the sandbox is down (502 from API), retry later and notify your instructor with timestamp.

docs.title: WebSocket / comments not working
docs.text: • Some campus networks block WebSockets—try another network or ask IT to allow wss:// to the API host.

docs.title: Wrong time on deadlines
docs.text: • Confirm your system clock; course policy may define timezone for due dates.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Environments
  • Incident response (for admins)
